_comment: Christmas carols and songs, own arrangements (L1 plan, Task 9). Specs and references: tools/arrangements/christmas.py. Two main candidates were rejected (see 'rejected') and replaced by the two spares of the task, o-christmas-tree and the-first-noel.

pieces.title: Jolly Old Saint Nicholas
pieces.tempoSource: editorial: 96, a steady beginner pace for the source's 'Lively' (the 1881 printing has no metronome mark)
pieces.levelNote: Level 1: right hand in one position on D (D to A, the B as the one extension, like Twinkle's A), single notes; left hand single notes and three open fifths in G position (G2 to D3); heuristic proposes 2 (score 2.14); no published syllabus placement exists for this arrangement, and the eighth-note density raises the score just over the first cut (1.76)
pieces.notes: Arranged in G major (the 1881 source is in A major). Right hand single notes from D4 to B4; left hand half notes on G, A, B, C and D with open fifths at the start, the middle and the end. The words are Emily Huntington Miller's 1865 poem; the music is generally attributed to James R. Murray (School Chimes, 1874).

reference.description: Franklin Square Song Collection [No. 1], ed. J. P. McCaskey (Harper & Brothers, 1881), p. 80, soprano line, A major; same page on Wikimedia Commons (File:Jolly_old.gif)

pieces.title: Silent Night (Stille Nacht)
pieces.tempoSource: editorial: dotted quarter = 56 (quarter = 84), a calm lullaby pace; the reference score plays quarter = 60
pieces.levelNote: Level 2: the melody spans C4 to F5 in 6/8 with dotted rhythms, so the right hand changes position; left hand open fifths in four positions; heuristic proposes 3 (score 5.81); no published syllabus placement exists for this arrangement, and the proposal is the heuristic's known overrating of held left-hand fifths (the core arrangements of Amazing Grace, Greensleeves and Happy Birthday are also proposed at 3 and catalogued at 2)
pieces.notes: The contemporary melody in C major over open fifths on C, G and F, with a fifth on D under 'sleep in heavenly peace'.

reference.description: Score 'Contemporary' in the article (sounds in D major, 6/8)

pieces.title: Joy to the World
pieces.tempoSource: editorial: 96, a little under the \midi tempo of the reference score (quarter = 102)
pieces.levelNote: Level 2: D major (two sharps), the right hand descends a full octave and returns; left hand open fifths and single notes in D position; heuristic proposes 2 (score 3.44); no published syllabus placement exists for this arrangement
pieces.notes: Lowell Mason's tune Antioch in D major; the left hand stays around D3 to A3 with open fifths on D.

reference.description: Score in the article (Lowell Mason, The Modern Psalmist, 1839, No. 144), soprano, D major

pieces.title: O Come, All Ye Faithful (Adeste Fideles)
pieces.tempoSource: reference: the \midi tempo of the Wikipedia score (quarter = 90)
pieces.levelNote: Level 2: G major, the melody moves between D4 and D5 with position changes; left hand open fifths changing on beats 1 and 3; heuristic proposes 3 (score 5.43); no published syllabus placement exists for this arrangement, and the proposal is the heuristic's known overrating of held left-hand fifths (the core arrangements of Amazing Grace, Greensleeves and Happy Birthday are also proposed at 3 and catalogued at 2)
pieces.notes: The hymn tune in G major; the left hand plays open fifths and single notes, changing harmony at most twice a bar.

reference.description: Score in the article (four-part organ setting), upper voice, G major

pieces.title: Deck the Halls
pieces.tempoSource: editorial: 108, lively but manageable; the 1881 source gives no tempo
pieces.levelNote: Level 2: F major with dotted rhythms and running eighths in the fa-la-la refrains; left hand open fifths in four positions; heuristic proposes 3 (score 4.99); no published syllabus placement exists for this arrangement, and the proposal is the heuristic's known overrating of held left-hand fifths (the core arrangements of Amazing Grace, Greensleeves and Happy Birthday are also proposed at 3 and catalogued at 2)
pieces.notes: The 1881 version (without the middle fa-la-la of later versions), with its repeated second half written out. Left hand open fifths on F, C, G and B-flat.

reference.description: Franklin Square Song Collection [No. 1], ed. J. P. McCaskey (Harper & Brothers, 1881), p. 120, soprano line, F major

pieces.title: Good King Wenceslas
pieces.tempoSource: editorial: 100 (half note = 50), a walking carol pace; the source gives only a dynamic
pieces.levelNote: Level 2: G major, quarter-note melody over an octave (D4 to D5); left hand open fifths in several positions; heuristic proposes 3 (score 5.11); no published syllabus placement exists for this arrangement, and the proposal is the heuristic's known overrating of held left-hand fifths (the core arrangements of Amazing Grace, Greensleeves and Happy Birthday are also proposed at 3 and catalogued at 2)
pieces.notes: Arranged in G major (the source is in A major) in 4/4; the left hand plays open fifths on G, C, D, A and E.

reference.description: Christmas Carols New and Old, first series, ed. Bramley and Stainer (Novello), No. 10, p. 20, soprano line, A major

pieces.title: O Christmas Tree (O Tannenbaum)
pieces.tempoSource: reference: the \midi tempo of the Wikipedia score (quarter = 90)
pieces.levelNote: Level 2: G major in 3/4 with dotted rhythms, the melody spans D4 to E5; left hand open fifths and single notes; heuristic proposes 3 (score 4.81); no published syllabus placement exists for this arrangement, and the proposal is the heuristic's known overrating of held left-hand fifths (the core arrangements of Amazing Grace, Greensleeves and Happy Birthday are also proposed at 3 and catalogued at 2)
pieces.notes: Anschütz's 1824 tune with its middle section and the da capo written out; open fifths on G, A, C and D in the left hand.

reference.description: Score in the article's section on the melody (sung line, D.C. al fine), G major

pieces.title: The First Noel
pieces.tempoSource: editorial: 96, a moderate hymn pace; the source gives only a dynamic
pieces.levelNote: Level 2: D major (two sharps) in 3/4, verse and chorus, the melody spans D4 to D5; left hand open fifths in several positions; heuristic proposes 3 (score 6.19); no published syllabus placement exists for this arrangement, and the proposal is the heuristic's known overrating of held left-hand fifths (the core arrangements of Amazing Grace, Greensleeves and Happy Birthday are also proposed at 3 and catalogued at 2)
pieces.notes: Verse 1 and the chorus as printed by Bramley and Stainer, over open fifths on D, G, A and B.

reference.description: Christmas Carols New and Old, first series, ed. Bramley and Stainer (Novello), No. 6, pp. 12 and 13, soprano line, D major

rejected.reason: The tune as it is known today was first printed in 1935 (Arthur Warrell's arrangement, Oxford University Press); the 19th-century versions documented in the Wikipedia article and the Vaughan Williams Memorial Library use different tunes. That fails the 1928 publication cut-off for melodies, and no notated source from 1928 or earlier was found (no score on any of the 27 Wikipedia language editions). Replaced by the spare o-christmas-tree.

No notated public-domain source from 1928 or earlier was found: no score on the English Wikipedia or its 5 other language editions, the Internet Archive's full-text search finds the song only in books from 1948 onwards, and IMSLP has only a 2010 CC BY 3.0 arrangement. Hanby's first printing (1866, The Dove) is not online. Replaced by the spare the-first-noel.
